joyful1.title: 1st Joyful Mystery: The Annunciation
joyful1.verse: Behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and shalt bring forth a son; and thou shalt call his name Jesus.

joyful2.title: 2nd Joyful Mystery: The Visitation
joyful2.verse: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.

joyful3.title: 3rd Joyful Mystery: The Nativity
joyful3.verse: She brought forth her firstborn son, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.

joyful4.title: 4th Joyful Mystery: The Presentation in the Temple
joyful4.verse: They carried him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord.

joyful5.title: 5th Joyful Mystery: The Finding of Jesus in the Temple
joyful5.verse: They found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, hearing them, and asking them questions.

luminous1.title: 1st Luminous Mystery: The Baptism in the Jordan
luminous1.verse: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

luminous2.title: 2nd Luminous Mystery: The Wedding at Cana
luminous2.verse: Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye. This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee.

luminous3.title: 3rd Luminous Mystery: The Proclamation of the Kingdom
luminous3.verse: The kingdom of God is at hand: repent, and believe the gospel.

luminous4.title: 4th Luminous Mystery: The Transfiguration
luminous4.verse: His face did shine as the sun: and his garments became white as snow.

luminous5.title: 5th Luminous Mystery: The Institution of the Eucharist
luminous5.verse: This is my body, which is given for you: do this for a commemoration of me.

sorrowful1.title: 1st Sorrowful Mystery: The Agony in the Garden
sorrowful1.verse: My soul is sorrowful even unto death. Father, not my will, but thine be done.

sorrowful2.title: 2nd Sorrowful Mystery: The Scourging at the Pillar
sorrowful2.verse: Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him.

sorrowful3.title: 3rd Sorrowful Mystery: The Crowning with Thorns
sorrowful3.verse: And platting a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head.

sorrowful4.title: 4th Sorrowful Mystery: The Carrying of the Cross
sorrowful4.verse: Bearing his own cross, he went forth to that place called Calvary.

sorrowful5.title: 5th Sorrowful Mystery: The Crucifixion
sorrowful5.verse: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit. And bowing his head, he gave up the ghost.

glorious1.title: 1st Glorious Mystery: The Resurrection
glorious1.verse: He is risen, he is not here. Behold the place where they laid him.

glorious2.title: 2nd Glorious Mystery: The Ascension
glorious2.verse: He was taken up: and a cloud received him out of their sight.

glorious3.title: 3rd Glorious Mystery: The Descent of the Holy Spirit
glorious3.verse: They were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they began to speak.

glorious4.title: 4th Glorious Mystery: The Assumption of Mary
glorious4.verse: Mary hath been taken up into heaven; the angels rejoice.

glorious5.title: 5th Glorious Mystery: The Coronation of Mary
glorious5.verse: A great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.

howItWorks.title: How to pray the Rosary
howItWorks.intro: The Rosary is a meditation on the life of Christ through the eyes of Mary. A full Rosary is five decades; each decade is one Our Father, ten Hail Marys, and a Glory Be, prayed while meditating on a mystery.
howItWorks.step1: Make the Sign of the Cross and pray the Apostles' Creed.
howItWorks.step2: Pray one Our Father, three Hail Marys, and a Glory Be.
howItWorks.step3: Announce the first mystery, then pray one Our Father.
howItWorks.step4: Pray ten Hail Marys while meditating on the mystery.
howItWorks.step5: Pray a Glory Be (and, if you wish, the Fatima prayer).
howItWorks.step7: Conclude with the Hail Holy Queen and the Sign of the Cross.
howItWorks.mysteryDays: Joyful — Monday & Saturday · Sorrowful — Tuesday & Friday · Glorious — Wednesday & Sunday · Luminous — Thursday

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy policy
privacyPolicy.body: ROSARY has no accounts and no sign-up. Your rosary progress — the mystery you are on and how many rosaries you have completed — is saved only on this device, in your browser. Nothing is ever sent to a server, and there is no tracking, no analytics, and no cookies. Clearing your browser data resets your progress.
